rollout.learning_mask_semantics: Whole actor-owned interval, including actor-caused terminal; excludes any release/script/blend tick. Bootstrap independently forbids physical terminals and transitions into scripted reset.
rollout.GAE: Invalid intervals form return boundaries; script rewards/values removed with torch.where; compact selected storage supplies native PPO.
rollout.normalization_population: All valid recovery and flat transitions together; not full unmasked batch, not each task cohort.

ppo.loss_interpretation: Finite value loss alone neither establishes accurate critic fit nor direct actor-gradient competition. Actor and critic parameter gradients are clipped separately.

checkpoint_std.warning: Target command sigma is not measured wheel-speed sigma; finite PD, delay and plant response alter actual motor trajectories.

reward_alias_risk.critic_input: Actor frame plus physical privileged state; manual_context35 has no recovery_enabled, holding_rl, release_pending or domain identity.
owned_recovery_only_changes: Subtract one-unit peaks from pitch_exp and roll_exp
Apply height and quiet-velocity cost without support/phase exemption
Add orientation/angular-velocity densities; add leg/wheel-speed densities during hold only
reward_alias_risk.interpretation: This is reward/return context aliasing for the shared critic, and task-dependent extra costs for the actor. It is a demonstrated structural risk, not an established cause of current quality degradation.

minimum_controls: Parent-flat versus latest-recovery actor, identical initial state/terrain and deterministic mean action; each with signal delay disabled/enabled. Record command hold/release, holding gate streak and post-release metrics separately.

On identical latest actor means and delay setting, compare deterministic actions, current learned std, and restored parent std with matched random samples. This isolates noise from mean-policy change without a PPO update.

Before any shared-critic reward repair, capture valid recovery/flat cohort counts plus raw reward, returns, advantages mean/std and critic residual by cohort on the same frozen rollout; global loss cannot establish domination.
minimal_repair_conditions: If deterministic latest actor is healthy but current-std runs cannot maintain 1s stability, freeze an explicit exploration-std schedule or cap in a new contract; preserve original evaluation gates and masks. Select caps from the matched replay, not arbitrary tighter bounds.

If latest deterministic mean has regressed against parent under matched delay, use a preserved parent starting point for a revised continuous recovery run with qualified retention; do not roll back consumption accounting.

If cohort critic residuals substantiate hidden reward-context aliasing, align flat and recovery base reward semantics globally or make the context observable to critic in a reviewed contract. Do not reintroduce positive phase dwell bonuses or hot-edit production.
not_confirmed: Whether current actor deterministic mean is worse than parent
How much learned std versus signal-delay contributes to hold failure
Actual reward/return/advantage variance by valid cohort
Whether latest critic loss is driven by 200-cost terminals versus dense recovery costs
All nonwheel contacts as post-release failures
A causal claim that critic loss directly suppresses actor gradients
